subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — latency/throughput requirements (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Rafael —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're aligned on the decision path between Hosted API and Dedicated capacity.

Recap of what you shared (please correct if I've mis-summarized):
- Workload: realtime checkout fraud scoring + contextual merchant messaging
- Typical request size: ~250 tokens per request (avg)
- Peak concurrency target: 600 concurrent requests (spiky around US business hours)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~100k requests/day (~70 RPS average, peaks to ~700 RPS for short bursts)
- Latency targets: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 200ms (hard requirement for checkout flow is p99 < 200ms)
- Security: no PHI, but must meet corporate audit and single-tenant isolation preference for production

Immediate ask from your side: confirm whether you need Dedicated capacity for SLA/predictable latency or if Hosted API with reserved throughput and caching is acceptable for an initial pilot.

Attached: finpay-sizing.xlsx (my sizing notes from today's call). I flagged two configurations that look promising.

Recommendation (short):
- For pilot/proof-of-concept: we can validate on Hosted API while configuring intelligent batching and prefix KV cache (gives lower cost and faster iteration). Hosted can meet p50/p95 in many cases but p99 during large bursts is where Dedicated usually helps.
- For production (if p99 < 200ms under sustained/bursty load is required): Dedicated capacity gives predictable tail-latency and isolation; we can size GPU pool and reserve burst capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm whether you'd like a Hosted pilot or want us to size Dedicated for a 2-week performance trial (which we can run in your account/tenant).
2) If Dedicated: share expected monthly RPS 95th/99th percentiles, peak window duration, and any procurement contacts so we can build a formal quote.
3) If Hosted: we'll provide a tuning runbook + expected cost range and a short benchmark test harness to run against your sample traffic.

Can you confirm the preferred path and an internal decision date (e.g., this week / next week)?

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: finpay-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet — recommended GPU pool sizing & workload assumptions)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — latency/throughput requirements (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Marissa —

That summary is spot on. A couple clarifications from our end:
- The checkout flow is the highest priority for p99 — if that fails we see conversion impact. We consider p99 < 200ms a hard requirement.
- Bursts: we see ~10–15 minute peak bursts during promo triggers where traffic jumps from ~120 RPS to ~700 RPS. Those happen several times per day.
- Security/procurement: procurement will prefer single-tenant / Dedicated for anything we classify as production if cost delta is within reason.

We're leaning toward Dedicated for production because of the p99 guarantees and isolation. That said, we'd like to:
1) do a quick Hosted benchmark to understand tuning and cost delta, and
2) run a short Dedicated trial to validate tail latency at production-like bursts.

Procurement contact: Maya Singh <maya.singh@finpay.com> (cc'ing in a separate email once I loop them). Our target decision date for pilot approach: 2026-02-24.

Can you send a ballpark for Dedicated monthly cost for the sizing in your spreadsheet and options for a 2-week trial + any required MSA addendum?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Product, FinPay
rafael.mendes@finpay.com
+1 617-555-3421

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — latency/throughput requirements (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Thanks Rafael — great, that timeline works. Quick follow-up and concrete next steps: 

1) Pilot plan recommendation
- Stage 1 (Hosted benchmark, 3 days): run traffic replay of 1 hour of peak traffic to measure p50/p95/p99 with caching/batching tuned. Deliverable: benchmark report + tuning checklist.
- Stage 2 (Dedicated trial, 2 weeks): provision a small Dedicated pool sized from finpay-sizing.xlsx and run production-like bursts. Deliverable: trial SLA report with p50/p95/p99 and tuning recommendations.

2) Ballpark pricing (high level ranges)
- Hosted benchmark + tuning: one-time professional-services effort (approx 8–12 hours) — USD 6k–9k.
- Dedicated monthly (initial pool to cover ~700 RPS bursts while keeping p99 <200ms): estimated USD 40k–65k/month depending on reserved vs burst config. Exact quote depends on final sizing and quantization profile. Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (ballpark tiers).

3) Legal / procurement
- We'll share a redlined MSA / trial addendum. For the trial we generally provide a short-term agreement; procurement typically signs that plus an order form.
- Please loop Maya and any procurement/legal contacts. I can get our legal/finance folks involved once we have procurement contact info.

4) Action items & timeline
- Rafael: please loop Maya and confirm decision date (you mentioned 2026-02-24).
- Marissa: I will schedule the Hosted benchmark and send the trial order form for Dedicated once procurement approves.
- Neha: can you prepare a short latency benchmark brief and include the expected KV cache/ batching parameters we'll test? (cc'd)

Attaching: latency-benchmark-brief.pdf and the pricing sheet.

If that all looks good I'll schedule the Hosted benchmark for next week and block time for the Dedicated trial prep.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
